summary: §6.3.1 line 9421 declares the cross-tab sign-out implementation: "All tabs/windows are signed out immediately (via SharedWorker or localStorage events)." The mixed alternation is also lossy — `SharedWorker` is a strict superset of capability vs. `localStorage` events; an honest spec asserts the contract and lets engineering choose.
recommendation: Replace line 9421 with: "Sign-out is propagated to all tabs / windows of the same browser within 100 ms (cross-tab) and to all devices of the same user within p95 ≤ 500 ms (cross-device, via Convex reactive subscription on `Session.revoked_at`). Implementation may use SharedWorker, BroadcastChannel, or `localStorage` events for cross-tab fan-out — engineering choice."

summary: Subdomain handling unauthored. Open questions: (a) can Org A claim `acme.com` and Org B claim `eu.acme.com` simultaneously (subdomain split)? (b) If Org A claims `acme.com`, are subdomains (`engineering.acme.com`) auto-included or must each be separately claimed? (c) Email-domain match for invitation auto-routing — is `@eu.acme.com` matched against an `acme.com` claim or only against a separate `eu.acme.com` claim? §48.6 covers shared-use detection in `m6_domain_shared_use_rejected` (gmail.com, hotmail.com, etc.) but the subdomain-vs-shared-use distinction is unauthored. Mid-market enterprises commonly hold `@subsidiary.acme.com` mailboxes; the silence is a real-world build blocker.
recommendation: Author in §48.6 a "Subdomain Resolution Rule" sub-section: (1) base-domain claim (`acme.com`) covers the registrable domain only; subdomains are not automatically included; (2) subdomain claim (`eu.acme.com`) is permitted concurrently with a base-domain claim by a different Org iff both claims successfully verify the DNS TXT record at their respective subdomain; (3) email-routing match is most-specific-domain-wins (an email at `@eu.acme.com` routes to the `eu.acme.com` claimant if one exists, else to the `acme.com` claimant if one exists, else unrouted); (4) base-domain claim by Org A blocks future subdomain claim by Org B unless Org B's subdomain is verifiable independently per (2).

summary: Console-bridge layer carries per-event DLQ webhook `console_bridge.dlq_entered` (filed as D-1.6-003 P1 for Appendix C / Appendix G registration) but lacks an aggregate failure-storm detector. Audit_Prompts.md Prompt §6.7 Check #5 explicitly requires "console bridge failure storm" anomaly detection wired to Appendix C. Without aggregate detection: (a) a Convex outage that DLQs 1,000 bridge events in 5 minutes generates 1,000 individual webhooks (per-Org webhook subscribers receive 1,000 noisy notifications, not one storm alert); (b) Ops have no consolidated surface to detect a bridge-layer melt-down before paging escalates; (c) the affected Buyer Org Owner cannot tell a single transient failure from a sustained outage. The §42.6.1 audit-integrity job catalog has no parallel "console-bridge-storm" detector job.
recommendation: Author §25.2.6 "Console-Bridge Failure Storm Detection" with: (a) detector definition — fire `console_bridge.dlq_storm` (per D-3.4-004 Appendix C entry) when EITHER (i) > 100 `console_bridge.dlq_entered` events per Org per hour OR (ii) > 1% of bridge events DLQ'd in a 15-minute rolling window OR (iii) DLQ depth > 1,000 events for any Org; (b) suppression rule — once `dlq_storm` fires for an Org, individual `dlq_entered` per-event webhooks are suppressed to that Org's webhook endpoint until the storm clears (storm clears when DLQ-rate falls below 10% of trigger threshold for 30 minutes); (c) Ops escalation — `dlq_storm` always pages Ops P2; persists > 30 min → P1; persists > 4 hours → P0; (d) §42.6.1 job catalog extension — a `console_bridge_storm_detector` Convex scheduled job runs every 60 seconds with cursor-based DLQ-rate computation; (e) per-Org and per-Bid-Workspace breakdown rendered on Ops Console §50.6.4 incident response surface; (f) acceptance criterion: storm detection latency p95 ≤ 90 seconds from threshold cross.
links: PHASE3.4_FINDINGS.md §3 Check #5; D-3.4-004 (paired Appendix C event); D-1.6-003 (per-event DLQ webhook); §25.2.4.

The acceptance criterion fails to say what consensus scoring means with N=1 (it is, definitionally, not consensus).
recommendation: Split §10.10 step 2 into two regime-bound sub-criteria: (a) Team Mode: minimum 2, maximum 5 Team Members per Requirement (consensus-scoring regime); (b) Solo Mode: exactly 1 scorer (the Workspace Owner), divergence detection suppressed per §13.6.2. summary: §10 is silent on Workspace transfer, archive, restore, and Workspace-Owner reassignment impacts on the pipeline phase. Specifically: (a) Workspace transferred between two Orgs (e.g., M&A) — does the pipeline phase reset, freeze, or carry forward? (b) Workspace archived mid-Phase-6 — is the bidding window paused or terminated? (c) Workspace restored after archive — does the bidding window resume from where it paused, or restart with a new minimum-7-day floor? (d) Workspace Owner deprovisioned and reassigned — do all in-flight gate validations re-run under the new Owner's permissions?
recommendation: Author §10.19 "Workspace Transfer / Archive / Restore Semantics" with: (a) transfer is forbidden mid-evaluation (Workspace must be at Phase 13 closed or archived); (b) archive freezes the pipeline phase, all timers pause, all webhooks throttle to a deferred class; (c) restore resumes the pipeline phase with timers re-anchored to `restored_at` (not `archived_at`), and the Phase 6 minimum-7-day floor re-applies if archive landed during Phase 6; (d) Workspace-Owner reassignment is allowed at any phase, all in-flight gate validations re-run under new Owner's `evaluation_owner_mode` and entitlements.

summary: Beyond the channel destination (D-11.2-008), the nightly-digest spec is silent on: (a) **cron schedule** ("nightly" — what local time? what timezone? (e) **reviewer-rotation cadence** — daily? weekly? quarterly? (f) **action on missed review** — escalation path? auto-revert? quarantine the PR-introduced auto-generated row? (g) **retention divergence** between the audit-trail emitter's log store (M.4.5 "lifetime of the spec repo") and the channel's native retention (Slack default retention is org-policy-dependent and bounded; an email DL has no retention by default).

summary: Override-target keying is by `{concept_name}` only — the override line format is `@appendix-m-internal-only: {concept_name} — {rationale}`. Triggered concepts emerge from the detector as `(concept_class, concept_name, spec_anchor)` tuples. Two distinct triggered concepts can share a `concept_name`: e.g., an enum value `solo` in `EvaluationOwnerMode` (Appendix J row) and a field named `solo` in some other entity; or two Appendix C webhook events with the same kind suffix in different domains. The override does not include the concept_class or spec_anchor, so binding an override line to a unique triggered concept is non-unique. The auto-row-generator's "appropriate spec-area group banner (inferred from the concept's spec anchor)" cannot resolve when the concept_name maps to two anchors.
recommendation: Amend the override grammar to require `{concept_class}::{concept_name}@{spec_anchor}` keying: `@appendix-m-internal-only: enum::EvaluationOwnerMode.solo@appendix-j-line-NNNN — internal-only construct, not surfaced (...)`. Update the parser, the example in §M.4.4, the comment template in §M.4.3, and the registered status strings in Appendix J.

location: Master Spec §M.4.2 trigger class #3 (Capability — non-AI; line 49405).

summary: The detector "operates on the post-edit Master Spec parse tree relative to the pre-edit snapshot. False positives on cosmetic edits (header level changes, anchor renames, prose rewrites without new concept introduction) are filtered by the parser; the gate fires only on structural insertions." The filter rule is implementation-defined. A heading-anchor rename (`{#feature-x}` → `{#feature-x-v2}`) is structurally a deletion + insertion at the parse-tree level; without a canonical cosmetic-edit classifier, the parser's behavior is opaque. Two CI runs against the same PR (e.g., on a re-trigger) might disagree on whether the edit is cosmetic. The detection rule needs to enumerate the cosmetic-edit patterns deterministically.
recommendation: Author a §M.4.2.1 sub-section enumerating the cosmetic-edit classifier as a deterministic rule set: (a) heading-anchor rename (anchor slug differs but heading text + body unchanged) — filtered; (b) heading-level change (`###` → `####` or vice versa, heading text + body unchanged) — filtered; (c) prose rewrite with no new field, no new table, no new acceptance-criteria block, no new enum value, no new spec-anchor — filtered; (d) anchor renumbering across an entire section (e.g., §13.x → §13.y) — filtered IFF the section's data-model and acceptance-criteria contents are byte-stable; (e) all other diffs — fire the gate. Codify the rule set in the parser spec for M02.3.

summary: §M.4.4 says the gate "auto-generates the corresponding Appendix M row in §M.1 marked `Internal-only, never surfaced` … places the row under the appropriate spec-area group banner (inferred from the concept's spec anchor), and commits the row update to the PR branch as part of the gate run." Two concurrent PRs A and B each invoke `@appendix-m-internal-only:` on different concepts that resolve to the same area-group banner. Both PRs auto-generate rows under that banner. Whichever PR merges second produces a structural merge conflict on the M.1 table — the post-merge state of M.1 from PR A's branch is unaware of PR B's appended row. The gate-run is local to a single PR branch; the conflict-resolution rule for concurrent diffs is undefined. M.4.4 is silent on whether the second-merging PR re-runs the gate against the post-A-merge M.1 state, fails the merge, or auto-rebases.
recommendation: Author a §M.4.4.1 sub-section pinning the concurrency rule: (a) each PR's gate run produces a `proposed_appendix_m_rows[]` patch; (b) on merge attempt, the gate re-runs against the post-merge M.1 state; (c) if a concurrent merge produced a structurally-conflicting row under the same area-group banner, the second-merging PR fails the merge with new status `appendix_m_coverage_on_diff: concurrent_area_group_conflict` and the PR author resolves via rebase + re-trigger. Register the new status in Appendix J per D-11.2-006.

summary: The gate parses the PR description for `@appendix-m-internal-only:` annotations. GitHub PR descriptions can be edited after submission, after the gate has run, after the gate has passed, even after merge in some configurations. §M.4.4 does not specify whether the canonical override snapshot is taken at (a) gate-run time (first push), (b) merge-time (final commit), (c) most-recent gate-trigger, or (d) the merge-commit's associated PR description. A late edit to the description can change the gate-run record without re-triggering the gate. The audit-trail emitter (§M.4.5) captures `override_annotations[]` at gate-run time, but if the PR description is edited later, the emitter's snapshot becomes stale relative to the merged state.
recommendation: Author a §M.4.4.2 sub-section pinning the snapshot semantics: (a) the canonical override snapshot is the PR description AT MERGE TIME (the commit SHA of the merge); (b) the gate re-runs on every PR-description edit AND on every push; (c) the audit-trail emitter records BOTH the at-merge-time snapshot AND the most-recent-pre-merge gate-run snapshot, and emits `appendix_m_coverage_on_diff: pr_description_drift` if the two differ.

location: Master Spec §M.4.3 inline-review comment poster identity (lines 49413–49420).
summary: §M.4.3 says "The PR check fails with status … and posts an inline review comment naming the missing concept(s) by anchor and concept class." The comment-poster identity is not declared — no github-app account, no signing key, no actor identifier. For audit-trail integrity per §6.7 Audit Ledger conventions, the actor performing an authoritative action (like blocking a merge with a posted comment) must be unambiguously identifiable. A PR reviewer cannot distinguish a real M.4 gate failure from a spoofed comment posted by an attacker with PR-write access.
recommendation: Pin the comment-poster identity to a named github-app (e.g., `sourcera-spec-gates[bot]`) with a documented signing key. Reference the github-app in §M.4.3. Add a `gate_run_signature` field to the M.4.5 audit-trail emitter that signs the gate-run record with the github-app's signing key.

summary: The gate depends on (a) GitHub API for posting the inline review comment, (b) GitHub API for auto-committing the override-generated Appendix M.1 row, (c) the structured log destination for audit-trail emission, (d) the integration channel for nightly digest delivery. §M.4 is silent on third-party outage semantics: if GitHub's API is degraded and the gate cannot post the comment, is the PR blocked (fail-closed) or allowed (fail-open)? If the log-destination is unreachable, does the gate fail or proceed without logging? If the integration channel is unreachable, does the nightly digest queue and retry, or skip? CLAUDE.md §12 Edge-Case Discipline enumerates third-party outage as a mandatory dimension; §M.4 covers none of it.
recommendation: Author a §M.4.7 sub-section pinning third-party outage semantics: (a) GitHub-comment-post failure: fail-CLOSED — PR is blocked from merge until the comment posts successfully (retry with exponential backoff for 1h, then page on-call SEV-3); (b) auto-commit failure: fail-CLOSED — PR is blocked, retry as above; (c) log-destination failure: fail-OPEN on the gate verdict but emit `appendix_m_coverage_on_diff_log_emission_failed` audit alarm at SEV-2; (d) integration-channel failure: the nightly digest queues to a DLQ with retry per §31 webhook conventions (5 retries, exponential backoff, then SEV-2 page).

summary: §48.5.3 AC #5 enforces buyer-anonymity at render time ("if `fully_anonymous`, the verification page MUST NOT contain the buyer Org name OR any direct identifier in HTML, JSON, OR meta tags") but is silent on the SIGNED `payload_canonical_json` — whose hash is rendered as a PDF provenance footer (line 35378) and whose contents are publicly verifiable via the JWKS at `https://verify.sourcera.io/.well-known/sourcera-cert-keys.json`. A literal reading freezes the buyer's full Org name into the signed payload at step 1, then renders the anonymized descriptor at step 2 — but the original full-name signature remains publicly verifiable forever via the JWKS verify endpoint. The temporal ordering of signing vs anonymity choice is implicit; AC #5's "in HTML, JSON, OR meta tags" arguably covers the verify endpoint's response JSON but the signed payload's hash + the JWKS-served public key let any reader reconstruct the original payload. No AC asserts the SIGNED payload's `buyer_org_display` mirrors the buyer's anonymity choice.
recommendation: (a) Reorder Workflow steps 1–2 so signing happens AFTER the buyer's anonymity choice is recorded, OR explicitly author a two-stage signing pattern: step 1 produces an internal-only draft hash, step 2's buyer-anonymity-choice triggers a re-derivation of `payload_canonical_json.buyer_org_display` per the chosen `buyer_anonymity_kind` and a re-signing under the same `signing_key_id`. QA test `m3_signed_payload_respects_anonymity_choice` asserts on every M3 publish path." (c) If the buyer changes `buyer_anonymity_kind` post-publish, re-sign with the new key (incrementing a `re_signed_count` field) — current spec has no provision for this.

location: §26.7.6 line 21321 Preview-Token Revocation — JWT key version scope
summary: Preview-token revocation is described as "flushes the JWT key version, invalidating all prior tokens" — but the JWT key version's scope is unspecified. Three interpretations are possible: (a) per-page (each SellerOrgPage has its own JWT key version; revocation flushes only that page's tokens); (b) per-Org (all preview tokens issued by any admin in the Seller Org are invalidated); (c) per-admin (only tokens issued by the revoking admin). Each has different security and operational consequences (e.g., interpretation (b) means revoking one page's leaked token also invalidates pending preview links for unrelated pages). §26.8.7 line 21503 references "bulk preview" tokens covering all SoftwarePages owned by a Seller Org — implying the JWT key may be Org-scoped — but this is not authoritatively stated.
recommendation: Author the JWT key-version scope explicitly. Recommend per-page scope (interpretation (a)): each SellerOrgPage carries its own `preview_jwt_key_version` integer; revocation increments the version, invalidating all prior tokens for that page only. Document in §26.7.6 and §6.7 Session Management. Update bulk preview in §26.8.7 to clarify that bulk preview issuance creates one token per SoftwarePage (signed with each page's current key version) — bulk revocation increments each affected page's key version atomically. Add Appendix I error code `seller_org_page_preview_token_key_version_mismatch` (HTTP 410).

summary: Cascade-pricing semantics unspecified in failure-mode #2. Prose: "Seller wins promoted auction then goes insolvent before settlement. Three coherent designs are unspecified: (i) **recursive second-price** — backfill bidder pays max(#3 bid, $500 floor); (ii) **cleared-price persistence** — backfill bidder pays the originally cleared #2 price (which equals their own bid); (iii) **own-bid pay** — backfill bidder pays their own bid (coincides with (ii) only by definition of second-price). Update §34.16.8 AC #2 QA test description to assert backfill cascade pricing with a 4-bidder fixture. location: Standard Events (lines 42423–42440) and Advanced Feature Events (lines 42446–42478)

location: Cohort assignment rules across Appendix G blocks
summary: §48.6 / §48.4.7 events that gate on k-anonymity carry explicit `k_anon_satisfied`, `cohort_size`, `floor`. §51 registers `usage_analytics_k_anon_floor_hit`. summary: Mirror contract is silent on whether free-text webhook payload fields (`reviewer_notes_text`, `denial_reason_text`, `revocation_reason_text`, `editorial_rationale_text`, `cancellation_reason_text`, `failure_reason_text`) propagate to PostHog event-level properties. Mirror events emit a SHA-256 truncated 12-hex hash of the free-text content as `<prop>_hash` (suffix replaces `_text` with `_hash`) for cohort-correlation without PII exposure. Numeric, enum, and ID-typed fields are propagated unchanged." Add CI gate `posthog_mirror_freetext_filter` enforcing the rule.

location: §6.8.5 AC #3 salt rotation (line 10375); §6.8.5 row #3 AIOperation content-hash columns (line 10351)

recommendation: Author a §6.8.5.x sub-section "Pseudonym Epoch Reconciliation" stating: (a) Pattern B User-row pseudonyms ARE rotated on salt rotation; (b) per-row scrubbed content-hash columns are NOT rotated (the source is destroyed; rotation is a no-op); (c) a `pseudonym_epoch_id` is stored on the User row to disambiguate which scrubbed-hash population is current; (d) audit operators querying multi-epoch chains use the User row's `pseudonym_epoch_id` to bind a query window.

summary: Manifestly-unfounded rejection appeal SLA undefined. Subject must file appeal within 30 calendar days, but the controller's adjudication SLA on the appeal itself is silent. A subject who appeals could be left in `manifestly_unfounded_rejected` indefinitely while the appeal sits unreviewed; the supervisory-authority complaint right (§6.8.6.2 line 10458) gives the subject a parallel external path, which keeps this at P2 rather than P0, but the internal appeal is procedurally toothless.
recommendation: Author §6.8.6.2.x "Appeal Procedure" specifying: (a) Appeal adjudication SLA = 30 calendar days from `appeal_filed_at`; (b) State-machine rows for `manifestly_unfounded_rejected → appeal_pending → appeal_upheld → in_progress` (re-opening the DSAR with a fresh 30-day clock) OR `appeal_pending → appeal_rejected_final` (DSAR remains terminal); (c) Subject notification at adjudication outcome including supervisory-authority complaint right re-statement; (d) Appeal adjudicator MUST NOT be the original Ops reviewer who flagged the request manifestly unfounded (separation of duties); (e) PostHog event `dsar.appeal_adjudication_completed` registered in Appendix G; AuditEvent emission per §6.7.

location: §37.1 Color Contrast row (line 31361) vs §3.11.3 Contrast Gate (line 3201) + WCAG 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast

Engineering reading §37 alone would build text-only contrast verification.

Non-text contrast (UI components, graphics, focus indicators) meets WCAG 1.4.11 per §3.11.3 (≥ 3:1 in both modes). Color is not sole information conveyor (WCAG 1.4.1)."

location: §37.1 Keyboard Navigation row (line 31362) vs §3.6.2 Focus Ring + §3.11.8 High Contrast Mode

location: §37 (whole) vs WCAG 2.1 AA Success Criteria 2.2.1 (Timing Adjustable) + 2.2.2 (Pause, Stop, Hide)

summary: §37.2 silent on (a) locale-resolution chain (URL `?lang=` param vs `User.locale` vs `Organization.default_locale` vs `Accept-Language` header vs browser default) — no precedence rule, no fallback chain; (b) `<html lang>` attribute (WCAG 3.1.1 Language of Page); (c) language-of-parts (WCAG 3.1.2); (d) pluralization rules (CLDR ICU MessageFormat); (e) number formatting beyond "thousands separator and decimal per locale" — negative-number rendering, percentages (relevant for §17 analytics), scientific notation, numeric input parsing.

Author §37.2.x "Pluralization & Number Formatting" sub-section bound to `next-intl` ICU MessageFormat with CLDR plural rules. Add `<html lang>` rendering requirement.

summary: Screen-reader announcement rate-limit rules scattered across the spec without an authoritative §37 home: §3.6.4 line 2424 (form errors, 2s), §3.6.4 line 2430 (character counter, 3s), §3.9.7 line 2956 (cursor presence, 2s), §3.10 line 3124 (bulk actions, 500/1000/complete-interval), §3.12.7 line 3445 (unread badge, 3s), §3.12.7 line 3446 (mentions, configurable assertive). summary: Tablet-floor disagreement across three sections. §38.1 says tablet = 640–1024 px (puts 640–768 in tablet). §38.6.1 says tablet = 768–1024 (puts 640–768 in `mobile_sm`). §3.4 says mobile = "viewport < 768px" (implies 640–768 is mobile). The §38.6 reconciliation note declares §38.6 authoritative ("§38.1 must be interpreted as a rounded narrative view"), but the §38.1 numeric is materially wrong and a junior engineer reading §38.1 alone would build tablet styles for 640–768 px when §38.6 contracts mobile_sm styles.

Replace §3.4 line 2287 prose with "mobile devices (mobile_xs and mobile_sm tiers per §38.6.1)" and bind to §38.7 as the authoritative gesture-translation contract.

summary: §38 silent on five mobile edge cases: (a) iOS notch / Dynamic Island safe-area-inset policy on the bottom nav (no `padding-bottom: env(safe-area-inset-bottom)` rule); (b) iPad Stage Manager multitasking-introduced viewport thrash; (c) Samsung Z Flip half-folded posture (only "folded → mobile_xs / unfolded → tablet" named — half-folded undefined); (d) browser zoom that takes effective mobile_xs width below 320 CSS px (relevant to WCAG 1.4.10; see Phase 37 D-37-007); (e) iOS Low Power Mode / Reduced Data Mode impact on Convex viewport-aware fanout (§38.6.2 line 31506).

summary: UserUIPreference offline-queued tier updates have no idempotency contract. AC #5 says "Updated within 500ms of a tier transition (network permitting; offline queues the update)." If a user transits desktop → tablet → desktop in 300ms while offline, queued writes can flush out-of-order and persist `tablet` when the live tier is `desktop`. No `last-write-wins-by-client-timestamp` rule, no `idempotency_key`, no client-clock skew tolerance.
recommendation: Author §38.6.6 AC #5 amendment: "Offline-queued tier-update writes MUST carry a `client_observed_at` timestamp; on flush, the server applies last-write-wins by `client_observed_at`. Client-clock skew tolerance ≤ ±5 minutes; writes outside the window are rejected and the client is forced to re-emit with the live tier." Add deploy-time validator.

summary: §48.3.1 / §48.3.2 / §48.3.5 frame all signals as positive-direction (more → better). The audit-required counterfactual pass identifies four realistic failure modes the spec must address: (a) seller concentration in a category triggering buyer choice paralysis (Herfindahl-Hirschman Index > 0.25 → M11 ComparisonPage signal degradation); (b) algorithmic-content SEO penalty on M9–M13 pages (Google EEAT downgrade if content too templated); (c) KB-staleness drag on Match Score quality (S3 calibration loop is positive but doesn't account for KB decay or `staleness_state = 'expired'` entries); (d) Marketplace listing flooding (>200 sellers per category) degrading buyer browse-quality. None has a kill-switch / alert / remediation path defined in §48.3 (or §48.4 SIM, which is per-event abuse, not aggregate compounding decay).
recommendation: Author §48.3.6 (or §48.3.8 if buyer-side / cross-side claim 48.3.6 / 48.3.7) "Negative Network Effects Monitoring" enumerating ≥ 4 negative-direction signals: (i) `category_hhi_concentration_index_quarterly` (HHI > 0.25 raises P3 to `ops_growth_admin`; suspends M11 ComparisonPage refresh); (ii) `category_page_eeat_downgrade_detector_30d` (Google Search Console rank delta + impression delta + CTR delta combined; downgrade triggers M9 / M10 / M11 / M12 / M13 cadence pause); (iii) `seller_kb_staleness_drag_signal_per_seller_org` (% KB entries with `staleness_state ∈ {expired, warned}` × bid-close frequency); (iv) `category_listing_count_overflow_warning` (count > 200 → buyer browse-quality regression alert). Each with threshold / paging owner / remediation path / dashboard tile.
links: PHASE48.3_FINDINGS.md F-NET-13; §48.4 SIM (per-event scope); §22 KB staleness state.

summary: Attribution-window taxonomy missing for cross-loop signals. Multiple §48.3.2 / §48.3.5 signals depend on multi-month cohort observation with inconsistent attribution windows: 30d (most signals), 60d (S5 secondary "to-paid-upgrade conversion within 60 days"), 90d (M16 retention rate; S5 "approved within prior 90 days"), lifetime (S6 grant→activation). §48.4 anti-spam framework references attribution-window expiry alerts but no master attribution-window taxonomy table exists for §48.3 signals. Without a taxonomy, the same loop measured from two dashboards could yield different numbers, and the Reverse-ETL pipeline build will produce diverging joins across signals.
recommendation: Author §48.3.2.1 "Attribution-Window Taxonomy" with a 4-band table: (i) Immediate (real-time signals: `signal_freshness_seconds_max ≤ 60s`); (ii) Operational (rolling-30-day signals); (iii) Strategic (rolling-90-day signals); (iv) Lifetime (lifetime cohort signals). Per-signal mapping table assigning each §48.3.2 + §48.3.5 signal to a band. Reverse-ETL pipelines join only within-band signals; cross-band joins require explicit signal-fusion documentation.
links: PHASE48.3_FINDINGS.md F-NET-14; §48.4 attribution-window expiry alerts; §51.1.3 event-naming normalization analog.

KB Spec §6.6 explicitly states: "Tools: full toolset (needs `read`, `bash` for docling, `write` for structured output). **No MCP needed at ingestion stage.**" §22.10.6 narrows to "Full `agent_toolset_20260401` enabled (needs `read`, `bash` for `docling`, `write` for structured output). `mcp_toolset` `sourcera_kb` — narrowed to the bootstrap/ingestion surface: `kb_dedupe_check` (§22.8.4.9, `always_allow`, read-only similarity probe) and `kb_entry_draft_create` (§22.8.4.8, `scoped_allow_with_quota`, per-session write cap of 200 drafts per parent AIOperation). The parse stage runs locally against the uploaded file; the persist stage calls `kb_entry_draft_create` per candidate entry with `created_via=ghost_rfp_ingestion` and `source_refs` populated from the uploaded file hash + in-document offsets. All other KB MCP tools are excluded." This is a deliberate Master Spec correction (the Reviewer-Inbox routing contract per §22.4.1 + the Ghost-Bid Importer Flow per §22.14.4 REQUIRE the ingestion agent to write KBEntry drafts via the MCP server — KB §6.6's "no MCP" was inconsistent with KB Spec §10.4's own flow diagram showing `ghost_rfp_ingestion agent parses` followed by KB entry creation). But the divergence is silent: §22.10.6 does not flag the change as an Authored Extension; `_integration/AUTHORED_EXTENSIONS_LEDGER.md` carries no AE row for the §22.10.6 MCP surface scope extension. Same convention violation pattern as D-5.2-006 (§22.8 9-vs-7 tool extension), D-5.3-010 (§22.12.6 / .7 / §22.11.2 schema closures), D-5.3-011 (§22.12.5 ghost-bid scope extension). Distinct from D-5.2-006 because that targeted the §22.8 tool-count divergence (KB Spec authoring an undefined tool); D-KB18-013 targets the §22.10.6 agent-allowlist deliberate divergence from a KB Spec explicit negative statement ("No MCP needed").
recommendation: Amend §22.10.6 tool allowlist row to include the in-line Authored Extension note: "Authored Extension — KB Spec §6.6 said 'No MCP needed at ingestion stage'; Master Spec adds `kb_dedupe_check` + `kb_entry_draft_create` to support the §22.4.1 Reviewer-Inbox routing contract for ghost-bid-ingestion-originated KBEntry drafts. The KB Spec §10.4 flow showed `kb_bootstrap agent runs` as the KB-entry-writing step; v7.0.0 integration consolidated KBEntry writes under the canonical `kb_entry_draft_create` MCP tool callable from both `kb_bootstrap` and `ghost_rfp_ingestion` agents." Add an AE row in `_integration/AUTHORED_EXTENSIONS_LEDGER.md` paired with the §22.10.3 KB Bootstrap MCP scope extension (which also extended KB Spec §6.3). Bundle ratification with v7.1.1 AE Ledger pass.
links: D-5.2-006 (§22.8 tool-count divergence; different scope); D-5.3-010 / D-5.3-011 (sibling AE-flag-gap defects); `_integration/AUTHORED_EXTENSIONS_LEDGER.md`.

location: `Sourcera_Master_Spec.md` §4.8.3 AIWallet entity field table — `monthly_included_value_dollars` and sibling `*_value_dollars` fields (line 8395 and adjacent)
summary: The AIWallet entity carries fields named `*_value_dollars` but stored as Integer cents (per §4.8.3 narrative: "Monthly included budget in integer USD cents"). This is a naming-vs-storage drift distinct from the Phase 1 `Decimal(10,2) USD` migration scope tracked under D-DEC-001 (E-1 Currency Unit Convention). D-DEC-001's recommendation targets the Decimal(10,2) → integer cents migration but does not address the inverse case where the field is already integer cents but mis-named "dollars". A junior engineer reading the field name in isolation would assume USD-unit storage and write Stripe Charge integration code dividing by 100 erroneously; a more careful engineer reading the §4.8.3 narrative learns the storage is cents and inverts. The two readings disagree on serialization unit.
recommendation: Either (a) rename `*_value_dollars` fields on AIWallet (and any sibling entities) to `*_value_cents` to align with §44.4.5 `*_usd_cents` convention and unambiguously reflect storage unit; or (b) author a single-source naming rule in §4 preamble or in the Glossary (Appendix K) explicitly defining "value_dollars" as "stored as Integer cents; rendered as dollars at the surface layer" and acknowledging the naming-vs-storage convention. **Recommend (a)** — the cents convention should propagate everywhere; D-DEC-001 closure already requires Phase 1 entities migrate to cents, and AIWallet should align. Add deploy-time validator `wallet_field_naming_cents_convention`. ~12 lines edits across §4.8.3 + sibling sections. Refines D-DEC-001 scope.
links: §4.8.3 line 8395; D-DEC-001 (parent); E-1 Decisions row; D-V711-002 (sibling — numeric supersession).
